title: Palak Paneer Spinach Cottage Cheese

seo.imageAlt: A vibrant bowl of homemade Palak Paneer, an Indian spinach and cottage cheese curry, garnished with fresh cream.
seo.imageCaption: Enjoy this creamy and flavorful Palak Paneer, a classic Indian vegetarian dish made with fresh spinach puree and soft paneer cubes.

description: Palak Paneer is a quintessential Indian dish featuring tender cubes of paneer Indian cottage cheese simmered in a vibrant, spiced spinach puree. This healthy and hearty vegetarian curry offers a delightful balance of earthy flavors and creamy textures. It is a beloved comfort food, perfect for serving with naan, roti, or rice.

instructions.title: Blanch and Puree the Spinach
instructions.text: Wash the fresh spinach thoroughly. Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil, then add the spinach and blanch for 2-3 minutes until wilted. Immediately transfer the blanched spinach to an ice bath to stop the cooking process and preserve its vibrant green color. Drain well and blend the spinach with green chilies and a splash of water into a smooth puree. Set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Paneer
instructions.text: Cut the paneer into 1-inch cubes. You can shallow fry or pan-fry the paneer cubes in a little oil until light golden brown for a slightly firmer texture, or use them directly. If frying, immediately transfer the fried paneer to warm water for a few minutes to keep them soft, then drain.

instructions.title: Saute Aromatics
instructions.text: Heat oil or ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan or kadai over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and let them splutter. Then add the finely chopped onion and sauté until it turns translucent and light golden brown, about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Add Ginger-Garlic and Spices
instructions.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste to the pan and sauté for another minute until the raw aroma disappears. Stir in the turmeric powder and coriander powder. Cook for 30 seconds, ensuring the spices do not burn.

instructions.title: Incorporate Tomato Puree
instructions.text: Pour in the tomato puree. Cook the mixture, stirring occasionally, until the oil starts to separate from the masala, which indicates the tomatoes are well cooked and the flavors have melded. This usually takes about 5-7 minutes.

instructions.title: Combine Spinach and Paneer
instructions.text: Add the prepared spinach puree to the pan and mix well with the masala. Add salt to taste and stir. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer. Add the paneer cubes and garam masala, stirring gently to combine. Cook for another 5-7 minutes on low heat, allowing the flavors to meld. Do not overcook the spinach or paneer.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Once the Palak Paneer has simmered and the flavors are well combined, remove from heat. If desired, swirl in a tablespoon of fresh cream for extra richness and garnish with a drizzle of cream or a small dollop before serving. Serve hot with naan, roti, paratha, or steamed basmati rice.

tips: For a smoother spinach puree, ensure you blanch the spinach thoroughly and blend until no large pieces remain. You can strain it through a fine-mesh sieve if you prefer a restaurant-style silky texture.
If your paneer is hard, soak it in warm water for 15-20 minutes before dicing to make it soft and tender, which will absorb the flavors better during cooking.
Avoid overcooking the spinach puree after adding it to the masala. Cooking it for too long can cause the spinach to lose its vibrant green color and some of its nutritional value.
